layeredWallDisplay.finding: A convincing Yunnan wall needs separate core mass, visible surface, base or plinth, corner or opening edge, repair and weathering layers.

colorAndAging.finding: Earth walls use restrained warm earth families with large, soft value shifts. Rain streaks, lower-wall dampening, faded zones and repairs create secondary variation.

masonryContrast.finding: Stone or brick bases, corner bands and opening surrounds may contrast with the earth wall, but their use is building-class and case dependent.

surfaceRelief.finding: Large geometric loss, medium-scale surface deformation, normal-map relief and base-color staining must remain distinct channels.

openingHierarchy.finding: External elevations tend toward sparse, small and high openings, while courtyard elevations can be more open. Exact opening types remain typology-specific.

moisture-resistant lower band and visual weight
quoins, brick corners, masonry frames or timber jambs

weatheringRules: Use large soft masks before adding small granular variation.
Increase moisture and darkening near the wall base and drainage routes.
Keep sheltered zones under eaves drier and darker where reference supports it.
Separate repair color from natural weathering color.
Keep all random fields deterministic per wall and building seed.
Exclude modern service boxes, cables, plants and scan holes from the historical base layer.

baseColor: moss or deposits when historically appropriate

ordinaryCourtyardDwelling.default: earth or plaster wall with restrained stone base and sparse exterior openings

unresolved: earth mix, lift height and compaction method
precise historical opening hardware and closure states
qaRequirements: wall core, finish, base, edge, repair and weathering can be toggled independently
weathering is deterministic and spatially coherent
lower-wall dampening follows ground and drainage context

scan boundary artifacts do not create authored wall damage
exterior and courtyard wall openness follow typology rules
large-angle rotation preserves correct wall and opening depth occlusion
